analysis.title: Perspectives Economics, November/December 2026
key_insights: US Q3 GDP accelerated to 0.8% quarter on quarter (non-annualised) from 0.6% in Q2. Growth is broadening beyond AI, with business investment outside AI growing moderately after being very weak in 2024 and 2025. Residential construction remains in recession.
US private consumption rose 0.9% in Q3, unchanged from Q2. Swiss Life attributes this to wealth effects from this year's AI-driven equity rally. It raised its US growth forecasts.

US September inflation surprised to the upside and became broader. Core inflation rose from 2.5% to 2.6%. Wage growth is cooling and the labour market is not overheating. Swiss Life left its inflation forecasts unchanged and expects only a gradual rise in US key interest rates.
Eurozone Q3 GDP grew 0.4% q/q. Excluding Ireland's volatile contribution, growth was 0.2%, in line with expectations. Germany +0.2% and Spain +0.6% grew, France -0.1% contracted and Italy stagnated.

Eurozone September inflation was 3.8%, slightly above expectations, driven mainly by energy. Core inflation rose to 2.5% from 2.4% in August, with no sign of pronounced second-round effects. The ECB left rates unchanged.

The ECB bank lending survey shows tighter credit conditions and lower credit demand in Q3 2026. This supports the ECB's cautious stance on further rate hikes. France has tightened noticeably while Italy has eased.

Germany Q3 GDP surprised at +0.2% despite higher inflation, low Rhine water levels and weaker foreign trade. October ifo and PMI readings point to continued momentum into Q4. Capacity utilisation jumped for capital goods and new orders are strong, which suggests fiscal spending is having a broader effect. Services, construction and property remain weaker because of higher interest rates.

German consumer prices fell slightly in September thanks to a temporary fuel discount. Energy prices hit new highs in October, which will raise future inflation. There is little pass-through to non-energy prices so far.

France contracted in Q3. Private and public investment were weak, French banks tightened lending more than European peers, and export demand fell sharply. Consumer confidence fell in October to its lowest since June 2013, and manufacturing PMI showed a slump in domestic orders.
French inflation was 3.4% in October. Energy prices rose 24.1% y/y and perishable food 8%, while processed goods prices were below a year ago.

Chart of the month: rising concerns about France's fiscal outlook have pushed the 10-year yield to 5%. France's debt ratio of 116% of GDP is not expected to fall over the next three years. The latest government bond issuance was oversubscribed two-fold.

Italy stagnated in Q3, driven by weak exports. Swiss Life cut its 2026 GDP forecast to 0.8% from 0.9% and left 2027 at 0.8%. October inflation was 5.4%, the highest since August 2023, and core inflation rose to 2.0% from 1.7%. Swiss Life raised its inflation forecasts to 3.3% for 2026 and 2.3% for 2027.

Spain Q3 GDP grew 0.6% on robust domestic demand, and Swiss Life raised its 2026 growth forecast to 2.5%. Inflation is 4.9%. Early elections on 29 November end Sánchez's minority government, and Spain has had no approved annual budget for three years.

Switzerland's Q3 GDP likely contracted slightly q/q after record Q2 growth, per SECO's weekly activity index. Swiss Life cut its 2026 growth forecast to 2.0%, and does not expect unemployment to fall. A preliminary Q3 GDP estimate is due 16 November.

Swiss inflation was 1.0% in September, with energy and fuels contributing 0.6 points. Second-round effects largely failed to materialise. The trade-weighted franc has risen about 2% since early October, which dampens inflation. Swiss Life expects 0.8% inflation in 2027.

UK autumn budget (Chancellor Healey's first) was in line with expectations and had little market impact. Fiscal headroom nearly halved because of higher interest costs in the OBR deficit forecasts. A small tax package centred on bank tax increases was presented.

UK August monthly GDP grew 0.1%, above expectations, led by manufacturing. UK September inflation was 3.5%, above Swiss Life's forecast, driven by petrol and air fares. Core inflation rose only moderately, so there are no noteworthy second-round effects yet. Swiss Life expects growth to slow after Q3.

China Q3 GDP growth was 4.5%, slightly above expectations. High-tech industrial production is up about 14% year to date, while real estate and infrastructure investment stay weak. The accelerated 'Six Networks' programme targets about 3% of cumulative GDP across transport, energy, water and digital networks. It is targeted and small, so it is not expected to change the growth trajectory, and Swiss Life sees growth of around 4.5% this year and next.
China producer prices rose 5.0% y/y on energy, metals and coal prices, tech demand and the heating season. Limited cost pass-through keeps consumer inflation low.

sector_views.rationale: Investment has declined almost continuously since Q2 2024 under high interest rates and contracted again in Q3.
High-tech industrial production is up about 14% year to date, well ahead of the rest of the economy.

risk_factors: Energy price surge triggering second-round effects, with early signs in Italian core inflation.
French fiscal outlook: 10-year yield at 5%, debt at 116% of GDP and no scenario of a decline in three years.
Tighter eurozone credit conditions, especially in France.
Weak US residential construction under high interest rates.
German services, construction and property weakness from higher rates, and low Rhine water levels.

Spanish political uncertainty and the lack of an approved budget.

charts_described: Chart of the month: France 10-year government bond yield at 5%, driven by fiscal concerns.
geopolitical: Geopolitical uncertainty and high energy prices weigh on the eurozone, which has still been growing robustly.
Geopolitical tensions have raised energy, metals and coal prices, driving China's producer price inflation.
French domestic political sentiment has worsened amid a wave of protests, and consumer confidence is at its lowest since June 2013.
Spain holds early parliamentary elections on 29 November after protests over housing costs, ending Sánchez's minority government.
